title: Redwood Data Retention & PII Controls Demo - Tempest Payments
summary: Redwood demo focused on data handling and retention controls: logging redaction, PII detection, request storage toggles, and KMS/HSM integration. Customer (Tempest) has strict PCI-adjacent requirements; key asks: ability to disable request storage per-route, automated PII redaction, audit logs for redaction events, and certs (SOC2/ISO). Agreed next steps: send security pack, run a scoped POC for 2 endpoints, and schedule a follow-up call to review audit logs and pricing.
action_items: Samantha Lee - Send SOC2 summary + security package (KMS, audit logs, encryption at rest) - 2026-08-07
Carlos Mendez - Prepare POC plan for 2 endpoints (3-week scope) and benchmark script - 2026-08-11
Omar Khan - Share current compliance checklist and redaction examples - 2026-08-06
next_steps: Redwood to send security docs and SOC2 artifacts
Schedule POC kickoff (3 weeks) to test request-storage toggles and redaction on staging
Run tokenized benchmark with Tempest sample prompts and share results
Follow-up meeting week of 2026-08-17 to review POC results and pricing options
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE); Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE); Nina Rao (Tempest - Head of Eng); Omar Khan (Tempest - Security); Jill Park (Tempest - PM)

[00:00] Samantha (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro on our side I'm Samantha, I run the AE for this vertical. with me is Carlos, our solution engineer.
[00:10] Carlos (Redwood): hi all, hey hey. super excited to walk through the data handling bits, we'll try to be pragmatic.
[00:18] Nina (Tempest): thanks, we mostly want to see how you handle PII and what toggles we get for request storage. we have PCI-adjacent regs and need to be careful.
[00:27] Omar (Tempest): and to add, our security team needs to see evidence of redaction logs and KMS integration; we also want SSO and RBAC details.
[00:35] Samantha: absolutely. quick agenda: demo console flows for data retention, show API flags for request storage off/on, then Carlos will demo redaction + audit trail, then Q&A and next steps. sound good?
[00:44] Jill (Tempest): yeah that's perfect.
[00:48] Carlos: ok I'm screen sharing now. sorry if my window pops up. first thing, here's the Console route config — you can toggle "store_requests": true/false at the route level. most customers flip this off for production if they don't want any request payloads stored.
[01:05] [01:06] Speaker 1: (inaudible) the toggle matches what we'd seen in the docs?
[01:10] Carlos: yep, the same. there's also a per-tenant default. we keep event-level audit logs even when store_requests is off, but those logs do not contain raw prompt text — they have metadata like request id, model, latency, and redaction markers.
[01:26] Nina: wait you said audit logs — will those show if a redaction happened and what fields were redacted?
[01:33] Carlos: good q. the audit entries show a redaction flag and a hashed placeholder like <REDACTED:EMAIL>. we do not store the original value when redaction is applied unless you opt into request storage.
[01:44] Omar: so if store_requests is off and redaction happens, there's no way to retrieve the original text later? that's important for our legal team.
[01:52] Carlos: correct, by design. if you need retrieval you must enable request storage and we recommend using customer-managed KMS so keys are under your control.
[01:59] [02:00] Samantha: small note: we can also do partial redaction where certain fields like name are redacted but non-sensitive context remains.
[02:08] Jill: curious how you detect PII — is it regex, ML, both? false positives can be a pain for us.
[02:15] Carlos: it's a hybrid. we run deterministic checks (regex for emails, cc-like patterns) first, then an ML classifier tuned for contextual PII — for ambiguous cases there's a confidence score and option to mask or tag for human review.
[02:27] Nina: and performance impact? we can't add a lot of latency to each request.
[02:32] Carlos: we aim for low overhead. redaction runs as a pre-processing pass and typically adds single-digit ms on our hosted infra; if you're on Dedicated/Private you can pin redaction to a separate lightweight service to keep inference fast.
[02:45] Omar: how do you prove compliance? we need SOC two artifacts, right? we require their SOC-2 type II and ISO certs.
[02:53] Samantha: yeah we'll share our SOC 2 summary and ISO overview. note: for Private deployments we can provide more detailed auditability and on-prem install.
[03:02] Nina: KMS integration — is it AWS KMS only? we use HashiCorp Vault for keys.
[03:07] Carlos: we support customer-managed KMS: AWS KMS, Google KMS, and HSM via external key interface. HashiCorp Vault is supported through our KMS bridge (you can rotate keys and bring-your-own-key).
[03:18] [03:20] Speaker 2 (minor crosstalk): I heard something about KV cache and how that persists, can you speak to that?
[03:26] Carlos: sure. KV cache is in-memory per model session and not persisted to disk by default. only when you enable request storage do we write any session content to persistent storage, and we never write raw KV objects unless explicitly requested.
[03:40] Nina: good. about retention windows — can we set retention by route or by model?
[03:45] Carlos: yes, retention policies are configurable by route, by tenant, or globally. you can set a TTL like 24 hours, 30 days, or disable retention (i.e., delete after processing).
[03:55] Jill: what's the deletion guarantee? is it immediate purge or background job? we need certs that data is irrecoverable.
[04:02] Carlos: deletions are immediate at the metadata level; object storage purge is handled by secure wipe jobs — for Dedicated/Private we can provide attestation logs for deletion.
[04:12] Omar: do you provide redaction logs that show before/after? our privacy team wants an explanation of transformations — not values but types and counts.
[04:21] Carlos: yes audit logs include transformation summary like "3 emails redacted, 1 cc-like token masked" with timestamps. no original PII recorded.
[04:29] Nina: competitor question — does this differ from how OpenAI handles it?
[04:33] Samantha: generally OpenAI stores prompts for improvement unless you pay for opt-out; Redwood gives route-level toggles and stronger enterprise controls (and private deployments) plus customer-managed KMS.
[04:45] Omar: they asked about Anthropic — are there any features they do better?
[04:49] Samantha: Anthropic has some built-in safety models; we focus more on serving and controls — you can layer their models on our runtime and still get our retention controls.
[04:59] Jill: can you demo the API call to disable storage? we want to see curl or SDK sample.
[05:05] Carlos: sure. switching to API view... example: POST /v1/requests with header X-Redwood-Store: false or sdk param store_requests=false. here's a sample curl — note the header and route id.
[05:25] [05:28] Carlos (reading): curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/requests" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Redwood-Store: false" -d '{"model":"rwd-2-large","input":"..."}'  // store disabled
[05:40] Nina: nice. if store is false and we later want to debug a failed request, is there an option to pull request content for a short window?
[05:48] Carlos: by default no — that's the point. you can enable a short retention window or request a temporary storage session for debugging (must be explicitly enabled and audited).
[05:58] Omar: what's the process for audit of those temporary sessions? who approves?
[06:03] Samantha: usually a security admin in your org triggers a temporary session; it's gated with SAML SSO + RBAC; all accesses are audited and require justification.
[06:13] Jill: how are redaction rules managed — do we edit regex in Console or do you provide a UI?
[06:18] Carlos: both. Console has a redaction rules editor and you can upload custom regex patterns, with a test pane to run sample inputs. we also support pushing rules via API for infra-as-code.
[06:29] Nina: can we integrate with our DLP pipeline? we want unified detection across systems.
[06:34] Carlos: yes, we can call out to your DLP via a webhook for human-review flows, or sync redaction events into your SIEM via our event export.
[06:44] Omar: any limitations on model features when redaction is on? e.g., embeddings or reranking?
[06:50] Carlos: embeddings are stateless and redaction runs before embedding generation; it's fine. reranking works as normal but we ensure no raw PII is forwarded to third-party services.
[06:59] [07:00] Speaker 3 (murmur): latency numbers?
[07:02] Carlos: typical gen latency is unchanged +5-10ms for redaction on hosted. Dedicated/private numbers depend on your infra but you can always offload redaction to a sidecar to avoid adding to critical path.
[07:15] Nina: can we get a short POC that hits two endpoints: (1) transaction enrichment which includes PAN-like tokens (obfuscated) and (2) dispute summarization where we need to redact emails and phone numbers?
[07:28] Samantha: yes, sounds reasonable. we'll scope 3 weeks: week 1 kickoff and data ingestion, week 2 run tests and redaction tuning, week 3 review and produce attestation logs.
[07:39] Omar: for the POC, we'll need to keep it in a staging VPC; can Redwood run in our VPC or do we need Private deployment?
[07:47] Carlos: for staging we can provision a Dedicated instance connected via VPC peering, or if you want full control we can do a Private deployment. Dedicated is quicker but Private gives you air-gapped control.
[07:58] Jill: cost differences?
[08:01] Samantha: Dedicated is committed capacity— lower per-token cost but requires commit; Private is a platform license + infra costs. we'll include ballpark pricing in the follow-up.
[08:10] Nina: ok. another question — retention TTLs for embeddings, do you store vector data if store_requests is off?
[08:16] Carlos: embeddings are stored as metadata only if you explicitly persist them; by default transient embeddings are allowed for immediate retrieval but not persisted. if you persist embedding store and want it encrypted with your KMS, that's supported.
[08:29] Omar: does Redwood provide redaction proof for auditors? like a report showing transformations?
[08:34] Carlos: yes we can generate a redaction attestation report that lists redaction events counts, timestamps, and anonymized examples.
[08:42] Nina: how about deletion on request? say a user invokes a GDPR right to be forgotten, can we delete all traces in Redwood?
[08:50] Carlos: yes, you can call the purge API and we will remove associated request content and references. the audit trail keeps a redaction/ deletion event but never the original content if store_requests=false.
[09:03] Jill: any weird gotchas if we use third-party models via your runtime?
[09:08] Samantha: you may need to check their policies; we block forwarding raw PII unless storage is enabled and you authorize it. some vendors have their own telemetry requirements — we'll surface those per model in the catalog.
[09:21] Omar: do you have client-side SDK helpers to pre-scrub sensitive tokens before sending?
[09:26] Carlos: yes, we have SDK hooks for preflight scrubbing and client-side redaction helpers.
[09:31] Nina: ok great. anything about function call logs and tools? we sometimes use tool-calling and don't want tool inputs persisted.
[09:39] Carlos: function/tool inputs follow the same store_requests toggle; additionally you can mark certain tool args as ephemeral in the schema so they never get logged.
[09:48] Jill: can you show where in Console to enable ephemeral args?
[09:52] Carlos: sure — go to tool settings, toggle ephemeral for the arg key, save; we'll show an entry that flags those in the audit stream.
[10:03] [10:05] Samantha: quick check on timeline — are you targeting production by Q4?
[10:09] Nina: yes ideally. we want security signoff in August and a pilot in September.
[10:14] Samantha: good we'll prioritize the POC.
[10:17] Carlos: switching to a quick demo of redaction evidence... here is a sample request where email and phone are detected, the UI highlights tokens and shows a masked preview. note: the transcript capture sometimes shows odd characters like K V cash in the auto transcript but it's just the KV cache.
[10:34] Omar: haha yes we saw that in previous notes.
[10:36] Carlos: also note we keep a redaction confidence score; low conf items can be routed to a manual review queue.
[10:45] Nina: we'd like to tune that based on our false positive tolerance.
[10:48] Carlos: absolutely — we'll include a tuning pass in the POC scope.
[10:53] Jill: can we get an example of the audit log line?
[10:57] Carlos (reading): {timestamp: "2026-08-05T15:00:23Z", route: "tx-enrich", event: "redaction", details: "email masked (count:2), phone masked (count:1)", user_id: "redacted"} — transcript sometimes flattens this to one-line entries.
[11:18] Nina: I see. will that log be exportable?
[11:22] Carlos: yes exports to your SIEM or S3 bucket; for Private we can ship logs to your internal endpoint.
[11:30] Omar: any encryption-in-transit specifics? TLS 1.2+?
[11:34] Samantha: we support TLS 1.2 and 1.3, mutual TLS available for private links, and SAML SSO for admin access.
[11:42] Jill: one more on redaction — can rules be versioned? we need to audit rule changes.
[11:47] Carlos: rule changes are versioned with an audit trail including the admin user who changed it and diff view.
[11:54] Nina: ok this is great. can you consolidate the security pack and an initial POC plan in an email?
[11:59] Samantha: yes I'll send the pack and proposed schedule.
[12:03] [12:05] Omar: who will be our technical point of contact?
[12:08] Samantha: Carlos will be the SE lead during the POC, and I'll manage the account.
[12:13] Carlos: yep happy to lead.
[12:15] Jill: thanks everyone.
[12:17] Samantha: quick recap: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO docs + KMS/HSM integration notes; Carlos to prepare POC scope for 2 endpoints and benchmark; Tempest to share sample redaction cases and compliance checklist. follow-up meeting week of Aug 17.
[12:33] Nina: thanks all, appreciate it.
[12:35] End of call.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings (K V cash for KV cache, S O C two spelled phonetically) and some automatic speaker labels; overall medium-quality auto-transcription.
